result.topic_en: Gauss describes the transverse Mercator (Soldner-type) projection with the meridian as principal circle for surveys extending mainly north–south, gives formulas for direction correction, true distance, geographic position and its inverse, and works the example of triangle 3 (Watten–Cassel–Fiefs) from the Base Métrique.
result.transcription:
18

Erstreckt sich die Meßung hauptsächlich längs des Meridians bei geringer Ausdehnung gegen Ost und West, so ist Mercator's Projection, den Meridian als Hauptkreis betrachtet, zweckmässiger
Die Hauptaufgaben sind hier folgende.
I. Verbesserung der Richtungslinie, wie sie berechnet ist
$\frac{(x'-x)(y'+2y)}{6rr}$
II. Wahre Distanz $=\sqrt{\{[(x'-x)^2+(y'-y)^2].[1-\frac{1}{3}\frac{(yy+yy'+y'y')}{rr}]\}}$ [-$+\frac{(x'\ldots)}{12\,rr}$-]
III. Geographische Lage
$\tang\lambda=\frac{y(1+\frac{yy}{6rr})}{r\cos(P-\frac{x}{r})}$ \quad $\tang\,\mathrm{Converg.\,Merid}=\frac{y}{r}(1-\frac{yy}{3rr})\tang(P-\frac{x}{r})$ \quad $\tang\frac{1}{2}(P-\frac{x}{r}-\psi)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{y}{r}(1-\frac{yy}{12rr})\tg\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Conv}.$
$\sin\,\mathrm{Converg\,Merid.}=\sin\lambda.\sin(P-\frac{x}{r})$
IV. Die umgekehrte Aufgabe.
[-$\frac{y}{r}$-] $y=r\sin\lambda\cos\psi.(1+\frac{yy}{3rr})$ \quad $\sin\,\mathrm{Converg.\,Merid.}=\frac{y(1+\frac{yy}{6rr})\tang\psi}{r}=\sin\lambda\sin\psi.(1+\frac{yy}{2rr})$
$\tang\,\mathrm{Converg\,merid.}=\tang\lambda.\sin\psi$

methods.what: Correction of direction (arc-to-chord reduction) in transverse Mercator projection
Geographic position (latitude-type angle) from projected coordinates
Half-angle relation for latitude difference and convergence
Inverse problem: projected ordinate from geographic position
Meridian convergence from λ and ψ
Numerical example: direction corrections and angles for triangle Watten–Cassel–Fiefs, using log computations

items.english: If the survey extends mainly along the meridian with little extent east and west, then Mercator's projection, taking the meridian as principal circle, is more suitable.
